sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Medical Device FDA 510(k) Filing and European CE Mark Compliance

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) signed between ARATS and SEF on June 29, 2010, effective January 1, 2011
Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion signed on August 9, 2012, effective February 1, 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (revised and effective January 1, 2025); Administrative Measures for the Registration of Beneficial Ownership Information (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective November 1, 2024); Regulations of the PRC on the Administration of Company Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, effective March 1, 2021); and applicable cross-strait investment protection rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan-registered investing parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Taiwan district notary public, followed by SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarial verification, which is the consular-legalization-equivalent path because Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Convention member. For documents issued in Apostille Convention member states, use a single-step Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority only, with no consular legalization chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan-registered investing parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notarization plus SEF/ARATS verification; this consular-legalization-equivalent path is mutually exclusive with Hague Apostille and must never be sequentially chained. If the issuing entity is in an Apostille Convention state, use a single Hague Apostille only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the WFOE incorporation and UBO filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan-registered investing parent, certified by the company secretary and Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notarization plus SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; no separate consular legalization or apostille should be added. For documents from Apostille Convention states, the path is a single apostille issued by the competent authority only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and latest amendments of the Taiwan-registered investing parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy from the Taiwan registry, notarized in Taiwan and verified through SEF/ARATS; this consular-legalization-equivalent route is used because Taiwan is not an Apostille party. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel paths and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Taiwan investing parent's commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan-licensed bank maintaining the parent company account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized in Taiwan, then verified through the SEF/ARATS cross-strait mechanism; this is the consular-legalization-equivalent path. If the issuing bank is located in an Apostille Convention state, use a single apostille only and do not add consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The WFOE applicant and all identifiable UBOs must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and PRC sanctions and export-control lists, including the Ministry of Commerce unreliable entity list and PBOC AML suspicious activity watchlist. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates, including source-of-wealth verification, beneficial ownership chain documentation, adverse-media checks, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Screening must be refreshed at onboarding, on material ownership changes, and quarterly thereafter; any positive sanction hit requires immediate Suspicious Transaction Report filing and asset freeze under applicable PRC AML and SAMR rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Declaration and Review System accessed through provincial integrated market regulation service portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A China WFOE Chinese-language name must follow the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or business characteristic plus enterprise legal form, for example Shanghai [Trade Name] Medical Technology Consulting Co., Ltd. Simplified Chinese characters are mandatory; traditional characters and full-width Latin letters are not permitted in the Chinese statutory name. An English transliteration may be registered for banking and invoicing purposes, but it must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration consistent with the Chinese name and must not create misleading similarity to government organs, international organizations, or existing protected names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, insurance, securities, trust, or fund without financial regulatory approval
Cross-Strait or Taiwan independence terminology creating political sensitivity
FDA, CE, or ministerial accreditation terms falsely implying government endorsement
Foreign country names and international organization names without special approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection notice from SAMR, the applicant has 15 days from receipt to file a written administrative reconsideration application with the immediately higher SAMR administration or with the people's government at the same level, under the Administrative Reconsideration Law. The appeal must cite the exact statutory basis for permissibility, attach revised name options, and, if necessary, request an oral hearing. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, an administrative lawsuit may be filed with the competent people's court within six months. For cross-strait investors, the authorized filing agent must hold a notarized power of attorney verified through the SEF/ARATS mechanism.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a China WFOE engaged in MedTech FDA and CE regulatory consulting under ISIC 749

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 7, 10, 23, 24, 27, 30, 31, 32, 33, 47 and Chapter IV; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4 and 8; Administrative Provisions on Registration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises (SAMR, effective 1 January 2020), Articles 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration in the proposed registered place, coordinated through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service; after license issuance the registration is recorded in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form (SAMR standard form) together with the Articles of Association and the resolution to establish the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No paid-up capital minimum and no blocked escrow account required for a WFOE in the ISIC 7490 consulting sector; the sole shareholder must still stipulate a registered capital amount in the Articles of Association and must fully pay the subscribed contribution within five years from the issue of the business license under Article 47 of the Companies Law. If the future expansion plan adds a restricted sector from the Foreign Investment Negative List, the relevant licensing regime may impose a minimum amount or a capital contribution schedule; absent such restriction, the contribution may be in cash, technology, or other lawful non-cash assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first meeting of the Board of Directors of [Company Name], a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company organized under the laws of the People's Republic of China, held on [Date] at [City], attended by all duly elected directors and constituting a valid quorum under the Company's Articles of Association. 1. Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company is USD [●], divided into [●] ordinary shares with a par value of USD [●] per share. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Taiwan Investor] is the sole subscriber and shareholder, and hereby subscribes to the entire registered capital, payable in cash or legal non-cash consideration in accordance with the contribution schedule contained in the Articles of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all contributions shall be paid in full no later than five years from the date of issuance of the Company's business license, as required by Article 47 of the Companies Law of the People's Republic of China, and any shorter period mandated by the foreign investment negative list or applicable industry regulations shall prevail; no escrow or blocked capital account is otherwise required for a professional consulting WFOE. 2. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open its primary bank accounts, including multi-currency operating accounts and online banking, with [Bank, Branch], and that [Name of Chairperson], [Name of General Manager], and [Name of Chief Financial Officer] are each authorized to open, maintain, sign for, and instruct such accounts. RESOLVED FURTHER, that payments below RMB [●] require one authorized signature, payments at or above RMB [●] require two authorized signatures, and all wire transfers supporting FDA 510(k) or European CE Mark regulatory consulting shall be effected only through bank-approved secure channels. 3. Registered Office Adoption. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be [●], being a commercial office lawfully available for company domicile, with a lease term of no less than twelve months, and that the registered office shall be the statutory address for service of process and official notices. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the legal representative is authorized to deliver the lease certificate, building ownership certificates, and landlord identity materials to the competent Market Regulation Administration for the adoption of the registered address. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Executive Director and General Manager, [Name] is appointed Supervisor, [Name] is appointed Legal Representative, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer. RESOLVED FURTHER, that each such officer accepts office and shall exercise the authority granted by law and by the Articles of Association, and that the Legal Representative is empowered to execute, deliver, and file all incorporation paperwork with the State Administration for Market Regulation, tax authorities, foreign exchange authorities, social security authorities, and banks. This resolution is irreducible and shall be inserted into the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise name pre-approval and business scope confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform and the local district Market Regulation Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the SAMR enterprise registration portal and verify that the proposed company name contains no prohibited trademarks, official designations, or misleading words and is distinguishable from existing registered enterprises. Select the company type as wholly foreign-owned enterprise with limited liability, populate the Taiwan investor corporate details, and specify the exact business scope as medical device regulatory affairs consulting and FDA 510(k) / European CE Mark compliance advisory under ISIC 7490. The system will screen the reserved name and generate a name pre-approval certificate. Submit the legal representative identity, the Taiwan investor's corporate authorization, and the intended registered address before finalizing the name reservation.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name pre-approval application
Taiwan investor's certificate of incorporation and legal existence certified copy
Power of attorney for the designated application filer
Legal representative identity certificate
Proposed business scope description and draft Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for collision, prohibited characters, or misleading industry wording, select two alternative names from the same portal and resubmit immediately; the SLA clock restarts only for the corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authentication of Taiwan investor documents and preparation of Chinese incorporation dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan district court-affiliated notary office, the provincial notary association performing cross-strait authentication, and the local Market Regulation Administration for document vetting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the WFOE Articles of Association, the sole shareholder's written investment decision, and the lease or ownership certificate for the proposed registered office. Have the Taiwan investor's certificate of incorporation, shareholder register, and board resolution notarized by a court-affiliated notary in Taiwan, then transmit a notarized copy to the relevant provincial notary association under cross-strait verification procedures for authentication before filing with SAMR. All Chinese translations must carry the translator's name, seal, and signature. Confirm that the lease term is at least twelve months and that the property is zoned for commercial office or consulting use, because SAMR and the local street-level supervision unit may inspect the site.
required_dossiers: Notarized and authenticated Taiwan investor incorporation documents
Shareholders' resolution to establish the WFOE and subscribe registered capital
Draft Articles of Association in Chinese
Registered office lease agreement and landlord title certificate
Translation attestation statement signed by the translator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authenticating notary association requires supplemental stamps, cross-references, or corrected seals, coordinate with the Taiwan notary to issue a corrected authentication letter and resubmit the entire certified package; incomplete certified copies will not be accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company establishment registration with SAMR and issuance of business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration with jurisdiction over the registered address, through the integrated enterprise registration online platform or physical service hall
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Company Establishment Registration Application Form, executed Articles of Association, shareholder qualification proof, legal representative and supervisor appointment resolutions, identity documents, and registered address proof. The registration officer will review the application for compliance with the 2023 Companies Law, the Foreign Investment Law, and the Foreign Investment Negative List. After approval, SAMR issues the business license bearing the unified social credit code. The legal representative must verify identity through face recognition or in-person signature. Concurrently confirm that the business scope clearly describes professional medical device regulatory consulting without implying manufacturing, import, or distribution activities that would require separate licensing.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration application form (SAMR prescribed format)
Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder
Certificate of incorporation and business license of the Taiwan investor
Legal representative and supervisor appointment resolutions
Identity certificates of the legal representative, supervisor, and financial officer
Registered office lease certificate and landlord identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a correction-required notice, cure the specified items within five working days through the same submission channel; if the application is rejected after three rounds, refile as a fresh substantial application with a new name reservation if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, social security, foreign exchange, and bank account registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local tax service hall, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, State Administration of Foreign Exchange branch through the designated bank, and a licensed commercial bank for the basic deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the business license, complete the mandatory one-stop post-incorporation registrations within the statutory deadlines. Perform tax registration and tax qualification filing with the local State Taxation Administration office; register the payroll and social insurance contribution account with the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; complete statistical reporting setup; and file the foreign exchange establishment registration with SAFE through the company's designated bank. Open the corporate basic deposit account in a licensed bank and instruct the bank to transmit account opening information to the People's Bank of China and SAFE. The Chief Financial Officer must adopt an accounting ledger and filing calendar for monthly and quarterly tax declarations.
required_dossiers: Original and copy of the business license
Legal representative identity certificate and company seal
Articles of Association and issuance resolution
Tax information supplement form prescribed by STA
Social insurance registration form and employee roster if staff are hired
FDI establishment declaration form and SAFE registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any post-incorporation registration is flagged for inconsistency, obtain the official discrepancy checklist, amend the internal record, and resubmit within the prescribed remedy period; statutory late-filing penalties are avoided by acknowledging the SAMR license date as the starting point.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal carving and public security filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB) and a PSB-licensed seal engraving enterprise under the Public Security Administration Measures for Seal Carving
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the legal representative must procure the company's common seal, contract seal, financial seal, and legal representative name seal from a seal carver authorized by the municipal Public Security Bureau. The engraver will require the original business license, identity certificate of the legal representative, and a written seal-carving authorization letter. Completed seal specimens must be filed with the local PSB, and the filing record should be retained in the corporate minute book. Banks and tax bureaus will require the financial seal and legal representative seal for wire transfers, invoices, and regulatory filings. The WFOE should also adopt an internal seal usage policy requiring approval from both the General Manager and the Legal Representative for contracts exceeding RMB [●].
required_dossiers: Business license original and duplicate
Legal representative identity certificate
Written authorization letter for seal engraving
PSB seal registration form
Internal seal use and custody policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the engraver refuses service or PSB stamping is delayed due to incomplete documents, obtain the exact missing-certificate list from the PSB and rectify within one working day; any non-compliant carved seal must be destroyed and recarved before bank account activation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; the ISIC 7490 business is pure MedTech regulatory consulting with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations. If future physical medical device production is undertaken, the competent authorities would be the Municipal Bureau of Industry and Information Technology and the local Market Regulation Administration for medical device production licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required for FDA 510(k) and European CE Mark regulatory compliance consulting under ISIC 7490.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - environmental licensing authority would be the Provincial Department of Ecology and Environment if a physical construction project is ever added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA registration and EIA report under the National Classification Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects because the current activity is office-based consulting under ISIC 7490.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater, zero VOC process emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation from the consulting activity; only ordinary domestic sewage and municipal solid waste are produced and are handled by municipal utilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the consulting activity itself; nonetheless, under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China and local building regulations, the leased office must be covered by a completed building fire-safety acceptance certificate or fire-safety inspection certificate, and the employer must complete occupational safety registration with the Emergency Management Bureau if any employees are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration, Taiwan, through the local National Taxation Bureau (NTB) with jurisdiction over the WFOE's registered address. Online electronic portals: MOF e-Tax Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw), MOF E-Invoice Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw), and MOEA Company and Commerce Registration Service (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain investment approval from the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Department of Investment Services under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; the Taiwan WFOE is foreign-owned and has no minimum capital obligation. Step 2: File company incorporation with MOEA using the Company and Commerce Registration Service (gcis.nat.gov.tw), submitting the articles of incorporation, Taiwan registered office address, shareholders and director list, and paid-in capital bank certificate if any. Step 3: The MOEA one-stop service transmits the incorporation record to the local National Taxation Bureau for mandatory business tax registration under Article 28 of the Business Tax Act; the WFOE is automatically assigned a Taiwan Unified Business Number (UBN) that is the TIN for corporate income tax, business tax, customs, and electronic invoices. Step 4: If the WFOE will issue standard VAT invoices, submit the Uniform Invoice User application to the local NTB and activate the Turnkey electronic invoice account on the MOF E-Invoice Platform. Step 5: Register the WFOE for bimonthly business tax returns and annual corporate income tax settlement under the Income Tax Act; appoint a local tax agent or accounting firm to administer filings. Step 6: Open a foreign-currency bank account with a Taiwan bank and register the exchange settlement account with the Central Bank of Taiwan under the Management of Foreign Exchange Act; this account is used to collect export consideration and to generate the foreign exchange settlement certificates needed for zero-rated export claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification elections; a WFOE is mandatorily treated as a resident corporate taxpayer and cannot elect pass-through status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (Taiwan VAT/Business Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: TWD 0/no turnover threshold: every business operator must apply for business tax registration before commencing business. The operational threshold for issuing standard 5% uniform invoices is average monthly sales exceeding TWD 200,000; at or below TWD 200,000, the WFOE may be classified as a small-scale business and taxed by assessment at 1% or 2% unless it elects to issue uniform invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan requires electronic uniform invoices for VAT-registered businesses. Invoices are issued from MOF-controlled serial-number blocks and transmitted via the certified Turnkey connection to the MOF E-Invoice Platform within the statutory transmission window, generally no later than 48 hours after issuance. The platform validates the invoice number, taxpayer UBN, amount, and tax code, then records the digital signature; there is no physical fiscal stamp, and anti-fraud control is achieved through encrypted XML submission, serial-number duplication checks, and e-Invoice platform reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 7 of the Business Tax Act zero-rates exports of goods and exports of services, including qualifying offshore services. The Taiwan WFOE's FDA 510(k) and CE Mark regulatory consulting services qualify as zero-rated exports when the customer is a non-resident, the service is performed for a foreign-market regulatory outcome, the benefit and use of the service occurs outside Taiwan, and the consideration is received in foreign currency and remitted to Taiwan. To substantiate the 0% rate, the WFOE must retain the service contract, foreign-currency invoice, evidence of service performance, and the bank's foreign exchange settlement certificate; periodic bimonthly business tax returns must reflect the zero-rated output tax and claim any input tax refund due.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry/Export Manifest) - mandatory where physical goods or regulatory samples are exported; for pure consulting services this document is substituted with the service contract and performance evidence.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill - mandatory for tangible exports of goods or samples; not required for the service-only FDA/CE consulting activity.
Commercial invoice / service agreement stating the foreign-resident customer, the FDA 510(k) or CE Mark compliance milestones, total consideration, and settlement currency.

Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (FIRC/Water Memo) issued by the Taiwan bank - evidencing inward remittance or settlement of foreign currency export proceeds into the WFOE's Taiwan bank account within the statutory deadline.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the WFOE cannot produce the export declaration (for goods) or the service contract, performance evidence, and foreign exchange settlement certificate (for services), the National Taxation Bureau will reverse the 0% export claim and assess output business tax at 5%, plus late interest from the original filing date. Under Articles 43 and 51 of the Business Tax Act, the underpayment is additionally penalized by up to three times the evaded tax. For fraudulent schemes, the Tax Collection Act and Business Tax Act impose criminal fines and imprisonment, and the assessment and recovery window is extended to seven years from the due date for intentional non-declaration, allowing retrospective clawback of previously allowed zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) acting through its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi remains only conditionally convertible under the capital account, although current account receipts and payments have been, in principle, freely convertible since China accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. An inward direct investment by a Taiwan-registered investor into a Mainland China WFOE is treated as foreign-direct-investment type capital, and the equity contribution must be remitted into a dedicated SAFE-registered FDI foreign exchange capital account; such funds cannot simply enter a basic RMB account before completing the foreign exchange registration and the foreign investment information reporting. Current account transactions, including cross-border consulting fees and royalties, are settled through licensed banks after authenticity review. Profit remittance by the WFOE to its Taiwan shareholder is permissible once the annual audit and final tax settlement are completed, withholding taxes have been paid, and a payment order with supporting tax certificates, audit report, and board resolution has been submitted to the bank. SAFE filing, real-demand verification, and regulatory approval are still required for large overseas disbursements, cross-border guarantees, foreign debt, and reinvestment. Therefore, the PBOC/SAFE framework restricts free fund navigability but provides a predictable compliance path for legitimate FDI and operating flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods exports, export proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic designated foreign exchange account within 90 days from the date of export customs declaration unless a deferred collection report is filed with SAFE; there is no mandatory conversion ratio, and the WFOE may retain 100 percent of eligible export proceeds in foreign exchange or settle all or part into RMB. For service-trade exports of medical device regulatory consulting under ISIC 7490, there is no surrender requirement, but every receipt must be booked through a licensed bank under the applicable SAFE current account transaction code, supported by the underlying contract and invoice, and reported through the SAFE cross-border receipt and payment monitoring system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account / Current Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account / Current Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account / Current Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account / Current Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very low viability; offshore fintech EMIs are legally barred from servicing a Mainland China WFOE as deposit-taking institutions. An offshore EMI cannot open an onshore RMB settlement account, cannot receive FDI capital contributions under SAFE rules, cannot perform FX settlement and sale business, and cannot satisfy China’s basic deposit account supervisory regime. The WFOE must hold its operating and treasury accounts at a SAFE-approved domestic bank. An EMI may only be considered as an ancillary offshore treasury wallet outside Mainland China and cannot be the primary clearing rail for capital injection, trade payments, or profit remittance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. The statutory legal representative of the WFOE must appear in person at the chosen bank branch to complete biometric onboarding, sign the basic deposit account agreement, and activate the FDI foreign exchange capital account. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a standard pathway for a Taiwan-resident legal representative. If the legal representative is unable to attend, the bank may permit a locally appointed financial controller to complete administrative filings only after a cross-strait notarized power of attorney has been verified and the legal representative has attended a live video interview; however, most major state-owned banks still require the legal representative’s physical in-branch visit before activating FX-related accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent beneficial ownership chain where the Taiwan shareholder is itself held through a multi-layer offshore vehicle or trust, creating concealment risk and an inability to identify the natural-person founders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unbroken ownership chart to each ultimate beneficial owner; Taiwan company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, and uniform invoice certificate; certified copies of passports or national identity cards for each UBO; cross-strait notary verification of corporate and personal documents; sworn source-of-wealth statement; and the PBOC beneficial ownership register filing in the bank’s prescribed format.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the FDI capital injection cannot be distinguished from circular, borrowed, or repatriated money, suggesting disguised hot money or unauthorized offshore leverage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements of the Taiwan investing company and UBOs; board resolution approving the investment; audit-certified financial statements of the investor; SWIFT MT103 or cross-strait remittance records evidencing first-provenance funds; signed equity subscription agreement; notarized loan or security documents if leverage exists; and a tax clearance certificate from the Taiwan competent tax authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical device regulatory compliance activity raises US/EU export control and sanctions concerns because the WFOE advises on FDA 510(k) filings and CE Mark approvals, potentially involving customers in restricted jurisdictions or dual-use technology content.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions screening against UN, US OFAC, EU consolidated, and UK consolidated lists; customer beneficial ownership declarations; end-use and intended-use statements for FDA/CE consulting deliverables; technology control plan and export-control classification assessment; contractual clauses prohibiting defense or military applications; and a compliance officer sign-off on each client engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Artificial consulting fee patterns or missing service substance, which could suggest trade-based money laundering through inflated regulatory consultancy invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed consulting agreements with clear milestones and deliverables; project files such as FDA 510(k) pre-submission minutes, CE technical documentation drafts, and notified-body correspondence; detailed invoices matching actual work performed; internal time records and project staffing reports; client bank payment records; and an independent auditor confirmation of revenue recognition.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder shall pass a board resolution, execute the equity subscription agreement, complete the foreign investment information reporting through the national investment information system, and file the FDI foreign exchange registration with SAFE through the receiving bank. The inward remittance must be sent via SWIFT MT103 from the Taiwan corporate bank account directly to the WFOE’s FDI foreign exchange capital account in the name of the WFOE, using the SAFE cross-border receipt and payment transaction classification code for inward direct investment equity contribution. Payment details must reference the WFOE’s registered name, the SAFE FDI registration number, and a clear purpose as equity injection; a third-party payer is prohibited. After receipt, the bank will perform capital verification against the registered total investment. If RMB working capital is needed, the WFOE shall settle the foreign exchange capital at the licensed bank and report the usage in compliance with the foreign investment negative list.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For FDA user fees, CE notified-body fees, subcontracted regulatory testing, and consultancy fees, the recommended clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 from the WFOE’s domestic account to the beneficiary’s bank, accompanied by the relevant SAFE service-trade transaction code, signed contract, invoice, and tax withholding certificates. For large equipment or laboratory purchases, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit opened by the domestic bank is appropriate. For incidental physical sample shipments, documentary collections may be used only when the counterparty trust level and document quality are high. All outbound service payments to non-resident beneficiaries require the WFOE to obtain the relevant tax clearance and withholding payment certificates from the tax authority before the bank releases the wire.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/CNY forward contracts covering identified current-account and FDI-related exposure with a SAFE-approved domestic bank under the real-demand principle
Plain-vanilla USD/CNY FX swaps for temporary liquidity conversion within the same operating cash-flow cycle
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term foreign-currency liabilities or trade finance exposure, supported by board-approved underlying debt
Onshore RMB/USD currency options where needed to cap adverse FX moves for approved trade flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore for this Mainland China WFOE; any offshore NDF must be executed only by the overseas parent and cannot be used to hedge the onshore entity’s CNY balance sheet

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership and control confirmation report pursuant to Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company and Commerce Registration Administration (MOEA-CCRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation window: 1 March to 31 March of every calendar year; event-driven updates for shareholding or control changes must be submitted within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The MOEA may order rectification by a fixed deadline; failure to remedy triggers fines of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 and continuing daily penalties of up to NT$50,000 until compliance; if the company ceases business for more than six consecutive months, administrative strike-off under Company Act Article 10 may be initiated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operation report of the foreign-invested enterprise filed by the overseas investor or the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May following each fiscal year end, unless an extension is expressly approved by MOEAIC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission may trigger administrative fines under the Regulations Governing the Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Overseas Chinese and Foreign Nationals; repeated default may lead to revocation of foreign investment approval and, if the enterprise is dormant for more than six months, administrative dissolution by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and final annual financial statements, including CPA certification where statutory thresholds are triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, through the local tax administration office with jurisdiction over the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 May of the year following the tax year for the annual final return and settlement filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a surcharge of up to 10% of the unpaid tax; late payment accrues an overdue fee of 1% for every two days after the initial grace period, capped at 15%; abandonment is evidenced by six months of cessation, which can be referred to MOEA for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders meeting: approval of the business report, financial statements, earnings distribution proposal, and filing of the approved documents and meeting minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company and Commerce Registration Administration (MOEA-CCRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary shareholders meeting must be held by 30 June of the following fiscal year; approved financial statements and meeting minutes must be filed with MOEA-CCRA within 15 days after the meeting where no exemption applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may be subject to fines of NT$20,000 to NT$500,000 for failure to convene or file; continued noncompliance combined with a six-month cessation of business may trigger administrative dissolution by MOEA under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance and update of statutory corporate records covering directors, supervisors, principal managers, registered office, share pledges, charges, and other encumbrances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registers are maintained at the registered office and are available for inspection by MOEA-CCRA, tax authorities, and shareholders; event-driven amendments are filed with MOEA-CCRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing annual obligation, with records required to be current as of 31 March for beneficial ownership reporting and as of 30 June for shareholders meeting approval; no separate annual filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or false register maintenance exposes responsible officers to administrative fines and inspection penalties; materially false books may be treated as false filings and, combined with inactivity for more than six months, support administrative strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory if any of the following applies: (i) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000, approximately US$1,000,000, under Company Act Article 20; (ii) the company is a public company listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange or Taipei Exchange, requiring annual consolidated financial statements audited by a CPA under Securities and Exchange Act Article 36; (iii) the enterprise is a bank, financial holding company, insurer, securities firm, futures commission merchant, or other financial institution designated by the FSC; (iv) annual operating revenue in the preceding full fiscal year exceeds NT$100,000,000, approximately US$3,300,000, requiring CPA certification or attestation of the profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and underlying financial statements; or (v) the Investment Commission of MOEA imposes CPA-audited financial statements as a condition of foreign investment approval. Taiwan has no general standalone headcount audit trigger, although headcount is used for SME classification and public-interest entity determinations under FSC rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS) as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public companies and WFOEs must comply with the Commercial Accounting Act and the Regulations on Handling Accounting Matters by Business Entities, and may apply Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards or the Taiwan SMEs Financial Reporting Standards (SME-GAAP). Income tax returns are prepared under the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Act with accounting records maintained under generally accepted accounting principles, including consolidated conversion under IFRS when group consolidation is required by the parent entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must identify natural persons who directly or indirectly hold 10% or more of the shares or voting rights or who otherwise exercise control, maintain a beneficial ownership file, and confirm the data online with MOEA-CCRA every year between 1 March and 31 March. Any change in shareholding, controllers, senior management, or other reportable beneficial ownership event must be reported within 15 days of the trigger event; a 30-day window is not recognized under Taiwan law. The report must be signed by the responsible person and kept available for regulatory inspection.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For the CN WFOE, the statutory Enterprise Income Tax headline rate is 25%; a preferential 15% rate applies on High/New Technology Enterprise certification and to qualified encouraged industries in Hainan Free Trade Port and Shanghai Lingang New Area; small low-profit enterprises within the annual taxable income thresholds are taxed at an effective reduced rate of 5%; qualified R&D expenses benefit from a 100% super deduction; income from qualifying technology transfers not exceeding RMB 5 million is exempt and 50% of the excess is taxable; certain qualified software and integrated-circuit enterprises are eligible for a 10% rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 (A-type), filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax System portal; required related schedules include A105000, A105070 and A107012 where relevant.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return, supplemented by quarterly advance Corporate Income Tax payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Enterprise Income Tax reconciliation return is due within five months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e. no later than 31 May for a calendar-year taxpayer; quarterly advance payments are due within fifteen days after the completion of each calendar quarter, i.e. 15 April, 15 July, 15 October and 15 January.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Revenue from Operations, including service fees received from MedTech clients for FDA 510(k) and European CE Mark regulatory consulting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the WFOE is incorporated in China, it is a Chinese tax resident and must report worldwide income. Gross revenue must include all fees charged in the ordinary course of regulatory consulting, including amounts invoiced through cross-border arrangement. No revenue may be excluded merely because the service is physically delivered to a non-resident client. If the WFOE charges a non-resident Taiwan affiliate, the consideration must satisfy the arm's length standard and contemporaneous documentation must support the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of Operations and Direct Cost of Services, including regulatory application fees, notified body certification costs, subcontract testing, technical review labor, and direct medical device engineering expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Direct costs paid to a Taiwan-related supplier or shared-service provider are allowable only if a written contract exists, economic services are actually rendered, the fees are at arm's length, and the WFOE retains sufficient evidence of the service receipt. Amounts lacking economic substance, duplicate-cost allocation, or unsupported cross-border invoicing must be added back in the reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and Surcharges: stamp duty, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, property tax and other business taxes that are allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Value Added Tax collected from clients is not an income tax deduction but is excluded from revenue. Imported VAT paid on cross-border services from Taiwan may be recoverable or creditable only with valid special VAT invoices or completed withholding tax payment vouchers, depending on the transaction. Cross-border service payments subject to VAT withholding must be documented to avoid the related payment being disallowed for Enterprise Income Tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, Administrative and Financial Expenses, including salaries, rent, legal and professional fees, bank charges, depreciation, amortization, foreign exchange losses and bad debt allowances claimed under the relevant deduction rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees, technology royalties and intra-group service charges paid to the Taiwan parent or affiliated service companies are not automatically deductible. In China, related-party management fees are not deductible where no actual service is identified; the payment must be the result of an arm's length arrangement, must not be duplicated in the group, and the Taiwan recipient must demonstrate actual cost and activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule A105000 Adjustments: add-backs and reductions for non-deductible related-party charges, entertainment expense ceilings, penalties, fines, interest on tax arrears, excess donations, thin-capitalization interest, and other permanent/temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE makes royalty, interest, or consulting payments to the Taiwan investor in the form of deductible fees that are actually hidden distributions of profit, the tax authorities will recharacterize those payments as dividends. The interest add-back threshold is exceeded when debt-to-equity above 2:1 produces interest on excessive related-party debt. Such recharacterization triggers withholding tax on outbound dividend or passive income in addition to the Corporate Income Tax correction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income after Loss Carryforward: accounting profit plus schedule adjustments, reduced by qualifying prior-year losses not older than five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE may use historical net operating losses carried forward for a maximum of five years, subject to the 100% loss utilization limits and continuity of ownership and business. Losses from offshore branches are not deductible against China-source income unless recognizably utilized under a valid foreign tax credit mechanism. The non-resident investor cannot deduct its own Taiwan losses in the WFOE's China return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable Corporate Income Tax Rate: 25%, 15% preferential, 10% special software/IC rate, or reduced rate for small low-profit enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the resident WFOE, the rate applied in this box is the entity-level rate on taxable income. This is distinct from the final withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to the Taiwan non-resident shareholder. The WFOE must verify the required qualifications and pre-filing certificates (High/New Technology, small low-profit, free-trade-zone encouraged industry) before applying a preferential rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate Income Tax Payable: Taxable Income multiplied by Applicable Tax Rate, then reduced by approved tax credits and preferential deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits may be used for foreign-source income taxes paid abroad other than on China-source income payable to Taiwan. Dividends distributed to the Taiwan parent are not deductible and do not reduce the Corporate Income Tax payable by the WFOE. Profit repatriation should be treated in the separate withholding tax schedule, not as an expense in Box 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance Corporate Income Tax payments already made during the year, including quarterly prepayments and any withholding on income paid by Chinese clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must reconcile the four quarterly advance payments against final annual liability; any balance due must be paid with the annual return. If any payments to the Taiwan parent were subject to withholding tax during the year, the withholding vouchers must be retained. Late prepayment interest is assessed if the quarterly estimates are understated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-Party Transactions Disclosure and Treaty Benefit Declaration: attachment of Schedule A105070 and declaration of beneficial ownership for the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Arrangement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any related-party transaction, regardless of amount, must be disclosed in the annual Enterprise Income Tax return. If the WFOE declares that the Taiwan parent qualifies for the reduced 5% dividend rate under the Cross-Strait double taxation arrangement, it must have the Tax Residency Certificate, evidence of beneficial ownership, board resolutions, shareholding records, the 365-day holding period verification, and substance evidence showing that the Taiwan recipient undertakes core income-generating activities in Taiwan.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return attracts a late-filing penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 per month or part thereof, increased to RMB 2,000 to RMB 50,000 after a tax authority warning; late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax, together with an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the tax that should have been paid if tax evasion is established under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63. Criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 can be applied where the deliberate omission is material, leading to criminal fines and imprisonment of up to seven years for the responsible representatives. Failure to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation also triggers a documentation penalty of up to RMB 100,000.
